Katalog Berita (Halaman 47/57)

#2134. Milan, Cardinale cambia rotta: gennaio occasione per rinforzare la rosa. Servono 3-4 acquisti

Sono finiti i tempi dei bilancini: Gerry Cardinale ha intenzione di spendere per il Milan. O almeno questo è quello che emerge dalle dichiarazioni del proprietario rossonero nell'intervista di ieri alla Gazzetta dello Sport. Sulla carta la nuova linea è tracciata, per competere con i grandi club europei (e della Premier League), il manager americano non vuole più farsi frenare da un prezzo elevato di un obiettivo di mercato ma vuole poterlo comprare con le risorse a disposizione. Qualcosa si è già visto quest'estate e i tifosi sperano che si continui a vedere, con maggior precisione e programmazione, anche nella sessione di mercato invernale.

C'è un passagio più di altri, dell'intervista di Gerry Cardinale di ieri, che spiega bene come è cambiato il modo di intendere l'investimento nel Milan da parte di RedBird. Il manager americano ha parlato così: "Sto facendo tutto il possibile per assicurarmi che, quando vogliamo un calciatore, nessuno possa dirmi: 'Non puoi prenderlo perché non potete permettervelo'. Adesso solo le società della Premier League sono in grado di investire certe somme e di assicurarsi i top player. Se voglio riportare il Milan ai vertici nelle coppe europee, non soltanto in Italia, dobbiamo capire come poter competere con i club più importanti al mondo". In questa manciata di periodi viene un po' riassunto il programma del nuovo Milan di Cardinale. Ci sono gli obiettivi, riportare il Milan al vertice italiano ed europeo, rendendolo abile di competere con i top club continentali; ci sono i mezzi per raggiungerlo, investire somme importanti per top player, senza farsi bloccare da paletti finanziari. Ovviamente per rendere tutto questo possibile, il Milan ha bisogno di sostenibilità finanziaria che si può raggiungere in vari modi, in primis lo stadio: "La forza trainante dietro a operazioni come questa è fornire al Milan la potenza finanziaria necessaria per competere sul mercato dei trasferimenti per assicurarsi i migliori giocatori al mondo. Trasformerò il profilo finanziario del club con le risorse che arriveranno dallo stadio, dall’arena a San Donato e dalle altre attività alle quali stiamo lavorando come Nba Europa".

Già nel corso dell'ultima estate, Gerry Cardinale ha fatto capire di non voler stare troppo a guardare. Neanche era aperto il mercato e aveva già speso oltre 100 milioni per Gonçalo Ramos e Mario Gila. Più avanti nella sessione ha personalmente voluto chiudere l'affare Diego Moreira per oltre 50 milioni. Da questo punto di vista l'aria è cambiata e c'è chi si chiede come mai per quattro anni si è continuato a tenere il freno a mano tirato, senza che Cardinale imponesse la sua visione (che dovrà essere verificata dai risultati, come è stata verificata negativamente quella delle ultime quattro stagioni in calando). Il mercato di gennaio rappresenta un'occasione per passare dalle parole ai fatti, un'opportunità per essere aggressivi sul mercato e dotare Ruben Amorim di altri giocatori che possano allungare ed elevare la qualità della rosa. Il Milan ha la necessità di trovare un attaccante da mettere in concorrenza o relazione con Ramos, ha l'obbligo di comprare un difensore centrale e di puntellare le risorse sulle corsie laterali. Sulla carta le parole di Gerry Cardinale possono far ben sperare: a gennaio si vedrà se questa carta si rivelerà solamente un'altra parola al vento o dei fatti che segnano realmente l'inizio di un nuovo ciclo.

#2133. Belgio-Italia, focus Inter: gli incastri che stuzzicano sui nerazzurri

Belgio-Italia, focus Inter: gli incastri che stuzzicano sui nerazzurri

La Nations League arriva al momento della verità e l'Italia di Roberto Mancini si prepara ad affrontare il Belgio nell'ultima giornata della fase a gironi. Questa sera, alle ore 20:45, gli Azzurri scenderanno in campo allo stadio Re Baldovino di Bruxelles con l'obiettivo di conquistare la qualificazione ai quarti di finale. La Nazionale arriva all'appuntamento forte del prestigioso 3-1 rifilato alla Francia a San Siro, risultato che ha portato l'Italia a quota 10 punti, in testa al girone insieme ai transalpini. Contro il Belgio, terzo a una sola lunghezza di distanza, basterà un pareggio per ottenere il passaggio del turno, mentre una vittoria garantirebbe il primo posto. I Diavoli Rossi, reduci dal successo sulla Turchia e già vittoriosi per 2-0 nella gara d'andata, sono invece obbligati a conquistare i tre punti.

Una sfida che presenta diversi motivi di interesse anche per i tifosi dell'Inter, con Alessandro Bastoni, Nicolò Barella, Federico Dimarco e Francesco Pio Esposito tra i protagonisti della spedizione azzurra. Riflettori puntati soprattutto su quest'ultimo, grande protagonista della vittoria contro la Francia grazie a una doppietta che ne ha confermato le qualità realizzative anche sul palcoscenico internazionale. Barella e Bastoni rappresentano due punti di riferimento dell'Italia di Mancini, mentre Dimarco può offrire soluzioni preziose sia nella costruzione del gioco sia negli ultimi metri. Il confronto con un Belgio che può contare su giocatori del calibro di De Bruyne, Doku e De Ketelaere promette una partita intensa, nella quale anche le prestazioni individuali potrebbero risultare decisive.

Se sei un nuovo utente per confrontare in maniera più completa le quote può essere utile analizzare anche l'eventuale bonus applicato dagli stessi operatori sui nuovi iscritti.

Tra i calciatori dell’Inter impegnati nella sfida tra Belgio e Italia, Nicolò Barella rappresenta uno dei profili più interessanti anche in ottica marcatori. Il centrocampista azzurro abbina inserimento, intensità e capacità di arrivare alla conclusione, caratteristiche che possono renderlo pericoloso soprattutto nelle partite ad alta intensità come quella di Bruxelles. In un match equilibrato, nel quale gli episodi possono fare la differenza, la possibilità che Barella trovi il gol merita attenzione anche sul piano delle quote. La rete di Barella è quotata 7.50 da bet365 e StarVegas, 6.10 da Vincitu e 8.00 da Eurobet. Un confronto che mostra valutazioni diverse tra gli operatori, con Eurobet che propone la quota più alta.

Se sei un nuovo utente per confrontare in maniera più completa le quote può essere utile analizzare anche l'eventuale bonus applicato dagli stessi operatori sui nuovi iscritti.

Un altro nome da seguire con particolare attenzione è Federico Dimarco, esterno che può incidere in modo determinante con la qualità del piede sinistro e la precisione nei cross. In una gara nella quale l’Italia cercherà di sfruttare anche le corsie laterali, il laterale nerazzurro può diventare un riferimento importante nella costruzione delle occasioni offensive. Proprio per questo il mercato assist lo vede tra i protagonisti più credibili della sfida. L’assist di Dimarco viene proposto a quota 3.10 da bet365, 4.50 da StarVegas e Vincitu, e 3.20 da Eurobet. Anche in questo caso le differenze tra i bookmaker sono evidenti, con StarVegas e Vincitu che offrono la valutazione più alta.

ITALIA (4-3-3): Donnarumma; Kayode, Scalvini, Bastoni, Calafiori; Doumbia, Tonali, Barella; S. Esposito, P. Esposito, Cambiaghi. CT. Mancini

Ma in que­sti giorni il serbo (che ha sal­tato anche la con­vo­ca­zione in nazio­nale) ha lavo­rato per recu­pe­rare e pre­sen­tarsi in gruppo domani alla ripresa della pre­pa­ra­zione del Milan.

E dopo un’estate in cui era finito ai mar­gini della squa­dra, prima di essere reinserito in gruppo. Dopo la sosta può essere pronto anche lui. Intervistato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, il giocatore del Como Kaiki Bruno ha parlato di Fabregas e svelato un retroscena su Ronaldo il Fenomeno:

Il Como l’aveva già cercata a gennaio prima di chiudere l’operazione in estate. Cosa le ha detto Fabregas per convincerla?

«Ho fatto alcune riunioni con lui prima di venire qui. Mi ha impressionato la sua idea di voler vincere sempre e la possibilità di poter crescere sotto la sua guida».

Qual è il consiglio più prezioso che le ha dato?

Sappiamo che dietro quei baffetti c’è una storia curiosa. Ce la racconta?

«Una delle mie prime partite da professionista con il Cruzeiro, avevo 18 anni. Alla fine, è comparso nello spogliatoio il presidente, Ronaldo, e ha salutato tutti. Poi mi ha stretto la mano, mi ha guardato e mi ha detto che i baffi mi stavano bene. Da allora non li ho più tagliati».

#2127. Mirabelli: "Calhanoglu centrocampista più completo d'Europa. Juve? Il mio amico Carnevali..."

Mirabelli: "Calhanoglu centrocampista più completo d'Europa. Juve? Il mio amico Carnevali..."

Nel corso di una lunga intervista a Tuttosport, Massimiliano Mirabelli, ora al Padova, ha parlato anche di Hakan Calhanoglu, corteggiato dalla Juventus perché in scadenza di contratto con l'Inter.

Tra le tante operazioni chiuse in rossonero, ce n’è una che la inorgoglisce ancora oggi?

�L’affare Calhanoglu. Senza alcun dubbio, la scommessa più bella e vincente della mia carriera. Parliamo di quello che, per me, resta ad oggi il centrocampista più completo d’Europa. Ha qualità incredibili, fuori dal comune».

Ci racconta da dove è nata quell’intuizione?

�Ho iniziato a seguirlo quando lavoravo all’Inter. Non riuscimmo a prelevarlo dal Leverkusen per via di una causa in atto relativa a un suo doppio tesseramento in età minorile che gli costò la squalifica. Per questo parlo di “scommessa”: lo volli a tutti i costi al Milan anche se non giocava da un anno ed era, di fatto, finito fuori dai radar. Fui criticato tantissimo. Ma, ripeto, ero convinto di avere tra le mani un ragazzo dall’enorme potenziale. La discussione più grande, poi, riguardava il suo ruolo. Spendemmo ore con Montella e - successivamente - con Gattuso per capire in che porzione di campo potesse esprimersi al meglio. A Leverkusen aveva giocato dovunque: da mezzala, da trequartista e pure da esterno. Inizialmente, lo abbiamo fatto giocare sulla corsia di sinistra, col piede invertito, per permettergli di accentrarsi e andare al tiro. Ma per me era chiaro che avesse tutti i requisiti per diventare un grandissimo regista. Quando lo suggerii a chi di dovere mi diedero del pazzo...».

Da lì una serie di annate altalenanti, prima che il Milan decidesse di “regalarlo” a parametro zero all’Inter...

�Non mi ci faccia pensare... Una roba indicibile, da non credere».

I discorsi con l’Inter per il rinnovo sembrano giunti su un binario morto. Tra i club alla finestra c’è pure la Juventus. Pensa che un colpo del genere potrebbe far svoltare il centrocampo bianconero?

�Assolutamente sì, ne sono convinto. Al mio amico Carnevali - con lui la Juve è in ottime mani - direi di prenderlo subito, senza pensarci un secondo. Sarebbe un affare clamoroso per la Juve come per lo stesso Calhanoglu. Ai bianconeri manca un calciatore dalle sue caratteristiche».

Eppure c’è chi ne storcerebbe il naso all’idea di vedere la Juve ingaggiare un profilo che a gennaio andrà per i 33...

�Per le qualità che ha può giocare e continuare a fare la differenza fino a 40 anni. Col passare degli anni acquisisce sempre più consapevolezza».

Che idea si è fatto sulla stagione dei bianconeri?

�Ci sono diverse carenze, ma non si può di certo puntare il dito contro Spalletti, che è un grandissimo allenatore. Uno da Juve. Ecco, non so se si può dire lo stesso dei calciatori che allena. Credo che nessun tecnico farebbe meglio di lui con questi giocatori. Nemmeno Guardiola, che è il migliore in circolazione. Se Luciano dovesse centrare il quarto posto farebbe un miracolo. A questa squadra mancano profili degni della storia della Juve. Di ciò che ha rappresentato per anni e anni in Italia e in Europa. Calhanoglu sarebbe un innesto cruciale. Il primo tassello del puzzle. Poi, però, andrebbero aggiunti gli altri...».

#2123. Come sta andando l'esperienza di Vincenzo Italiano da allenatore del Besiktas

L'ultima immagine di Vincenzo Italiano in Serie A è quella di un allenatore ormai conscio che il suo percorso al Bologna era finito. Lo avevano capito tutti, lui per primo, ma nessuno era abituato a vederlo senza la sua proverbiale grinta, quella fame con cui ha sempre guidato le sue squadre dalla panchina. In estate ha sfiorato il Napoli di Aurelio De Laurentiis, che ha però virato su Allegri e così lui ha scelto il Besiktas, accettando un contratto da 6 milioni di euro più bonus a stagione fino al 2028.

In Turchia il suo avvio è tutto sommato positivo, visto che è attualmente quarto in classifica. La Super Lig è un campionato molto particolare e sempre più competitivo, ma a Istanbul non gli hanno certo fatto mancare acquisti importanti, uno su tutti il suo bomber Dusan Vlahovic, sbocciato alla Fiorentina anche sotto la sua gestione. I punti di distacco dalla vetta occupata dal Galatasaray sono 6, con il Trabzonspor secondo a 3 lunghezze e l'Amed SK a +1. I presupposti sono ottimi.

Come sempre però il suo terreno di caccia sono le coppe. Nella sua carriera ha ottenuto i risultati migliori nei tornei a eliminazione diretta, chiedere a Fiorentina e soprattutto Bologna in caso di dubbi. Nella seconda competizione più importante per club del nostro continente Italiano ha privilegiato il turnover, ma questo non gli ha impedito di essere momentaneamente all'8° posto, che significherebbe ottavi di finale senza passare dai playoff, con 7 punti in 4 partite. Il pubblico di Istanbul lo ha già adottato e il coro a lui dedicato ne è la testimonianza.

#2118. Southampton will regret missing out on transfer deal for 25-year-old to Fulham: Opinion

Southampton were reportedly keen on luring the defender to St Mary’s in the last transfer window. However, they were beaten to the punch in the end by Premier League side Fulham.

Affengruber, 25, was snapped up by the London outfit on a four-year contract running until June 2028. He has since made seven league appearances for the Whites and has become a regular in their starting XI over recent weeks under the guidance of their head coach Alvaro Arbeloa.

The Austria international, who has three caps to his name so far in his career, was identified by the Saints as a potential replacement for Taylor Harwood-Bellis, who was sold to Aston Villa. However, a move to Hampshire wasn’t to be and Tonda Eckert’s side weren’t able to get a deal over the line in the end.

Southampton will rue not being able to land Affengruber following Keven Schlotterbeck’s recent injury that will see him ruled out for four to six weeks. They are now short of options at the back as they look to close the gap between them in the play-offs and the top two.

Southampton will have seen Affengruber as someone to bolster their defensive department. If he had joined them, he would have given them more competition and depth in his position.

The Saints will have to make do without Schlotterbeck over the coming weeks which isn’t ideal. Either Nottingham Forest loan man Zach Abbott or Nathan Wood will need to partner Jack Stephans in the heart of their backline.

Affengruber would have got plenty of game time under Eckert if he had linked up with the Championship side. He initially had to be patient at Fulham for his opportunity but he has now cemented his place in their team.

The Red Bull Salzburg academy graduate made his name at Sturm Graz. He then spent two years in Spain at Elche and played 84 games altogether, chipping in with two goals.

Southampton should sign a new defender in January. Affengruber is off the cards though after his recent emergence into the Fulham team.

Stephans isn’t getting any younger, Abbott could be recalled by Nottingham Forest and Wood has seen his minutes dry up. Therefore, they need someone to come in and perform next to Schlotterbeck when he returns.

The Saints lost 1-0 away at Preston North End last time out. They face Derby County at home after the international break.

"Penso che il giocatore sia sicuramente di valore poi la cosa che mi ha incuriosito dell'intervista di Mirabelli su Tuttosport è quando dice che ha un fisico tale che può giocare fino a 40 anni. Perché io invece dico che 6/6,5 mi sembrano già troppi: perché a giudicare dagli infortuni che ha avuto nell'ultimo anno e mezzo, secondo me è dura che arrivi fino a 40 anni. "Alla Juve. La Juve non ce l'ha uno come Calhanoglu. La Juve deve trovare un regista e un leader"

Calhanoglu dall'Inter alla Juve come Pirlo dal Milan alla Juve?

"Diciamo le cose come stanno, anche lì era una questione anche se non soprattutto di ingaggio. Tutti pensavano Pirlo fosse finito, lo pensavano Berlusconi, Allegri ma anche Antonio Conte e questo non l'ha chiarito nessuno perché Conte, all'inizio, Pirlo non l'aveva voluto. Fu una grande intuizione di mercato di Marotta, va riconosciuto questo, perché Conte non lo voleva all'inizio. Occhio a dire che Calhanoglu, come dico io, è in declino perché poi bisogna vedere. Intervenuto ai microfoni di Tuttosport, Massimiliano Mirabelli ha parlato della stagione della Juventus, lontana dai primissimi posti:

"Ci sono diverse carenze, ma non si può di certo puntare il dito contro Spalletti, che è un grandissimo allenatore. Uno da Juve. Ecco, non so se si può dire lo stesso dei calciatori che allena. A dirlo a La Gazzetta dello Sport è una leggenda del calcio belga come Vin­cenzo Scifo, ex di Inter e Torino e appunto simbolo dei Diavoli Rossi: "Man­cini sta facendo un lavoro molto inte­res­sante e gesti­sce bene il gruppo".

#2114. Stoke City won’t regret selling 27-year-old in the summer transfer window: Opinion

Stoke City cashed in on the attacker on 1st September and he penned a four-year deal at the MKM Stadium running until June 2030. Since leaving SCFC, he has made six appearances for the Tigers in all competitions and has chipped in with one assist.

Thomas, 27, was a key player for the Potters during his time at the Bet365 Stadium and was one of their key players under Mark Robins. He made 52 outings for the Staffordshire outfit in all competitions, scoring 10 goals laying on 15 assists for his ex-teammates.

Robins’ side haven’t missed him at all though and they are sat joint-top of the Championship table along with Birmingham City and Middlesbrough. They are positioned in 3rd on goal difference behind Boro and they are in the play-offs along with Wolves, West Brom, Swansea City, Southampton and QPR after 15 fixtures.

Stoke City won 2-1 away at Portsmouth last time out before the international break after goals by Jack McGlynn and Ben Wilmot. They are back in action next weekend at home to Birmingham City.

Stoke City have flourished since Thomas’ departure. SCFC are less reliant on one player and it has become more of a team effort.

The Wales international, who has 31 caps to his name, hasn’t been able to make the impact he would have wanted to at Hull City. He missed out on their recent squads against Brentford and Ipswich Town and was left on the bench last Saturday against Arsenal.

Thomas faces a tough battle to get into the Tigers’ starting XI in the top flight. They are positioned in 13th in the league and have adapted pretty well to the step up a division against the odds.

Stoke City signed the London-born man back in 2025. Prior to his switch, he had permanent spells at Boreham Wood and Huddersfield Town, as well as loans at Blackburn Rovers and FC Nantes.

Thomas was a great player for Stoke City and his numbers were very impressive. He deserved a big move to Hull City off the back of his form at SCFC.

However, the Potters are better off without him now and have others players stepping up. Robins’ men will be full of confidence at the moment and will be aiming to keep their momentum going against Birmingham City next Saturday.

#2112. La moglie di De Bruyne si lamenta: "A Napoli non può uscire. Ci diciamo che prima andiamo..."

La moglie di De Bruyne si lamenta: "A Napoli non può uscire. Ci diciamo che prima andiamo..."

Installa la nostra App gratuita e accedi più velocemente alle notizie

Mentre navighi nell'app, scorri il dito da sinistra a destra dello schermo per tornare alle pagine precedenti

Un ritorno in Belgio che sembra sempre più vicino. E per il Napoli le parole di Michelle De Bruyne, moglie di Kevin, suonano come un avvertimento. La moglie del centrocampista belga ha raccontato alla rivista NINA il disagio della vita in Italia, con le difficoltà del nazionale belga anche nel poter uscire e vivere normalmente lontano dal campo. "A Manchester la gente era ormai abituata e quasi non faceva caso a Kevin. Ma a Napoli è diverso. Ci diciamo che prima andiamo via e meglio è". Una situazione che alimenta la nostalgia di casa e la voglia di voltare pagina. "Certo, pensiamo insieme al futuro. E sempre più spesso ci diciamo: andremo a vivere qui nel Limburgo", ha dichiarato Michelle, 32 anni, sposata con il calciatore dal 2017.

A 35 anni, dopo una carriera straordinaria al Manchester City, De Bruyne era arrivato a Napoli nell'estate 2025 per aprire un nuovo capitolo. Ma l'esperienza italiana non ha rispettato le aspettative. I problemi fisici, le tensioni con Antonio Conte e le indiscrezioni sui contrasti con alcuni compagni hanno complicato il suo percorso. Neppure il cambio in panchina con l'arrivo di Allegri ha finora migliorato la situazione. Adesso anche le parole della moglie sembrano indicare una direzione precisa.

#2110. "Per 6 mesi non sarò calciatore": Kvaratskhelia diventa streamer, i momenti già virali

Durante il periodo di stop forzato a causa del grave infortunio, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia ha deciso di intraprendere una nuova attività sul web diventando uno streamer, su Twitch. Il georgiano ha avviato una serie di dirette per interagire con i propri sostenitori e magari ingannare il tempo in compagnia, durante il lungo percorso per tornare in campo.

La stella del Paris Saint-Germain ha condiviso con i propri followers dettagli riguardo ai tempi di recupero spiegando così la propria presenza sul web: "Per 6 mesi non sarò un calciatore", ha detto nel corso di una diretta. Nel corso delle sue trasmissioni in diretta non sono mancati momenti di condivisione e interazione diretta con i sostenitori, inclusi momenti di nostalgia come un abbraccio virtuale a un tifoso del Napoli che si è collegato.

Durante una delle sue dirette streaming ha ricevuto anche una telefonata inattesa da parte del compagno di squadra Achraf Hakimi. Kvara ha subito esaltato l'ex esterno dell'Inter davanti a tutti: "Questo è il miglior terzino sinistro della storia", ha detto del compagno. E ancora, una volta ha detto: "Il PSG è la squadra più forte di sempre, in campo e fuori".

#2109. Wolves should challenge Birmingham City and Middlesbrough for perfect Andre partner: Opinion

Wolves need to be keeping their options open for the January window despite a decent start to the season. Cesar Peixoto’s side currently sit 4th in the Championship and a good window will put them in a very strong position to push for automatic promotion.

Wolves should be keeping a close eye on Arthur Avom ahead of the January transfer window, with the Lorient midfielder offering an opportunity to strengthen their promotion push while potentially laying the foundations for a Premier League midfield.

The 21-year-old has emerged as an attractive target for several English clubs, with Birmingham City and Middlesbrough reportedly tracking his situation. However, Wolves should be looking to get ahead of their Championship rivals, particularly given the opportunity to negotiate a relatively affordable deal.

Avom has already established himself in French football, making 31 Ligue 1 appearances last season after helping Lorient win promotion from the second tier in 2024/25. He has continued to feature regularly this term and has also earned senior international recognition with Cameroon.

His contract situation makes the opportunity even more interesting. Lorient’s agreement with Avom currently runs until June 2027, potentially leaving the French club with limited leverage next summer.

The biggest attraction is how well Avom could complement Andre. Wolves already have an established midfield anchor in the Brazilian, who committed his future to the club until 2030 following relegation from the Premier League.

Andre provides defensive discipline, composure and the ability to dictate possession, whereas Avom offers greater mobility, energy and forward-running ability. The Cameroonian is comfortable winning possession, carrying the ball through midfield and contributing defensively, making him a natural candidate to operate alongside Andre in a double pivot.

That partnership could be particularly valuable across a demanding 46-game Championship campaign, allowing Andre to concentrate on controlling games while Avom supplies the athleticism and intensity needed to compete in both boxes.

There is also a longer-term argument for the move. Much of Wolves’ existing midfield group is already established, with Marshall Munetsi approaching 30 and Tommy Doyle and Boubacar Traore in their mid-twenties.

Avom would introduce another young option alongside Jordan James, helping reduce the need for an extensive midfield rebuild if promotion is secured. His experience in Ligue 1 and international football also means he would not necessarily need several seasons to adapt to a higher level.

Wolves cannot afford to overlook the immediate competition, either. Birmingham and Middlesbrough are both capable of offering attractive projects, while previous Premier League interest demonstrates Avom’s growing reputation.

If Wolves are serious about building a team capable of returning to the top flight and staying there, Avom is exactly the type of recruitment they should be considering. A January move could strengthen their promotion ambitions while giving them a potentially long-term partner for Andre.

#2104. West Ham should be keeping tabs on situation of out-of-favour Leeds United striker: Opinion

West Ham have a chance to propel themselves into title-winning contention in the January transfer window. WHU have been impressive to start the year and are the clear top scorers in the Championship, despite struggling to nail down a number nine.

West Ham United should be looking at Mateo Joseph as a potential January addition, with the Leeds United forward offering an interesting opportunity for Scott Parker as he looks to guide the Hammers back into the Premier League.

Parker has inherited a side with plenty of attacking quality, but the centre-forward position remains an area that could benefit from strengthening. With Joseph looking to be available in January, West Ham must be paying attention to his situation.

Joel Piroe has scored around four league goals since arriving on loan from Leeds, while Taty Castellanos has struggled to establish himself as a consistent goalscoring threat. West Ham are scoring freely, with 37 goals in their opening 15 Championship fixtures, but another option could prove important during the second half of the campaign.

Joseph would offer something different. The 23-year-old spent last season on loan at Mallorca, making 29 La Liga appearances, including 19 starts.

He registered two goals and three assists, with his underlying numbers suggesting there could be more to come from him in front of goal. His 4.92 expected goals compared with two actual strikes indicates that his finishing did not necessarily reflect the opportunities he found, according to FotMob.

Versatility is another attraction. Primarily a centre-forward or right winger, Joseph can operate across the frontline, giving Parker additional tactical flexibility. He also has experience of winning promotion from the Championship, having featured 39 times for Leeds during their successful 2024/25 campaign, recording three goals and three assists.

There is, however, an obvious complication. Joseph suffered an ACL injury while at Mallorca in April and has been recovering at Leeds. He is targeting a return to competitive action around January or February 2027, meaning any potential move would carry considerable fitness risk.

His modest senior goalscoring record also means West Ham would be taking a chance rather than signing an established Championship marksman. Nevertheless, that could make him an attainable target. Leeds are reportedly open to moving him on, while his injury situation could create an opportunity for a loan agreement with a potential obligation to buy.

West Ham need to be careful with their January recruitment, particularly with promotion within reach. However, Joseph’s age, versatility and previous Championship experience make him an intriguing option. If his recovery progresses as hoped, he could provide valuable competition for Piroe without requiring a significant initial investment.

#2103. Inter-Roma... finisce 6-4. L'analisi in 10 punti della "nostra" corsa scudetto

Non ce ne vogliano Lazio, Milan e Como. Ma oggi, per quel che ha mostrato fino a questo momento la Serie A, la sensazione è che nel momento caldo della stagione la corsa Scudetto possa ridursi a due sole contendenti. Inter e Roma. Per qualità della rosa, gioco espresso, attitudine al successo e interpretazioni dei singoli, ad oggi sono loro due le nostre candidate allo Scudetto con la possibilità di essere smentiti sul campo nelle prossime settimane. Fatta la doverosa premessa, eccoci qua al gioco che ci siamo proposti nella redazione di TuttoMercatoWeb.

- Portieri (ROMA) Pepo Martinez, Provedel e Di Gennaro da una parte. Svilar, Gollini e Vasquez dall'altra. Parte tutto da qui. La sfida a distanza fra Inter e Roma vede passare subito in vantaggio i giallorossi che con Svilar hanno probabilmente il miglior numero uno dell'intero campionato. Dopo la sosta rientrerà, dando un ulteriore boost di qualità alla rosa di Gasperini.

- Difensori (INTER) Il pareggio dell'Inter arriva presto. Qua almeno sulla carta non c'è storia, con i nerazzurri che per qualità ed esperienza ad alti livelli sono sopra ai giallorossi. Con Bisseck, Bastoni, Stones, Akanji, Pavard più il jolly Carlos Augusto, in pochi possono reggere il confronto a livello italiano. Non che la Roma sia messa male con Mancini, Ndicka ed Hermoso più il supporto di Balerdi, Ghilardi e Kourielakis, ma l'Inter vince questo confronto.

- Centrocampisti (INTER) Anche qua primeggia l'Inter. Per centrocampo si intendono i centrali ma pure gli esterni: Dimarco e lo Spence delle ultime uscite sono al top nel ruolo, anche se il confronto con Wesley e Molina non è così impari. Nel mezzo il top della Roma è senza dubbio Manu Kone, l'Inter risponde con i vari Calhanoglu, Barella, Zielinski, Sucic e via dicendo. Nel complesso meglio il reparto di Chivu.

- Attaccanti (INTER) La Roma ha il giocatore che ha segnato di più da inizio 2026 ad oggi. Ma l'Inter ha un pacchetto attaccanti ben più completo. Thuram e Lautaro ovviamente. Più Pio Esposito e Bonny. In Europa poche squadre possono permettersi tanta abbondanza tecnica. La Roma è strutturata diversamente, con Malen cannibale di gol e minuti e Dybala che quando sta bene è fra i migliori della Serie A. Quando sta bene, appunto. Vince l'Inter, ancora.

- Panchina (INTER) Parliamo di profondità della rosa, di possibilità di ruotare i titolari senza abbassare la qualità e di incisività a gara in corso con le sostituzioni. E anche qua ha la meglio Chivu, con scelte top in tutti i reparti, soprattutto a centrocampo. Ma anche le riserve, o presunte tali, di difesa e attacco sono di primissimo livello. Punto su cui alla Roma forse manca qualcosa.

- Allenatore (ROMA) Non ce ne voglia Chivu che ha vinto con grande merito l'ultimo scudetto. Ma il Gasperini che si sta vedendo in questa stagione a Roma sembra avere qualcosa in più, sorretto anche da una spinta motivazionale che potrebbe dare quel quid in più nel momento caldo della stagione.

- Ambiente e tifosi (ROMA) Questo è il punto probabilmente più controverso. O combattuto per meglio dire. L'Olimpico di parte giallorossa continua a macinare sold out ma pure il San Siro nerazzurro è contesto che spinge e regala sostegno. E allora a fare la differenza potrebbero essere le aspettative: perché dall'Inter strafavorita secondo tutti ci si aspetta quasi che debba vincere. Mentre per la Roma, non dovesse arrivare lo Scudetto, non sarebbe certamente un fallimento. E poi c'è l'entusiasmo: col passare delle giornate, quello di fede romanista potrebbe dare quel boost in più alla squadra di Gasperini.

- Società (INTER) Qua vince l'Inter per un ragionamento di struttura e continuità. Il tutto fa riferimento a Beppe Marotta, probabilmente il dirigente migliore che oggi il calcio italiano ha da offrire. La presenza dei Friedkin e il loro coinvolgimento nella Roma sono sempre più forti col passare delle stagioni, ma il comparto dirigenziale dell'Inter (anche con l'addio di Ausilio) resta fra i migliori a livello italiano. E non solo.

- Disponibilità sul mercato di gennaio (ROMA) Qua potrebbe spuntarla la Roma, con il fortissimo coinvolgimento di Gian Piero Gasperini nelle scelte dei rinforzi. Uno, forse due, arriveranno sicuramente. In casa Inter invece valutazioni ancora in corso, ma la possibilità che in inverno non saranno fatti nuovi acquisti esiste. Da qui il vantaggio dei giallorossi.

- Mentalità e abitudine al successo (INTER) Cose che non si possono insegnare e che si apprendono solo col tempo. L'Inter è al vertice in Italia e in Europa da anni, ecco perché è avanti rispetto alla Roma in questo singolo aspetto. Questioni, mentalità e abitudine alla vittoria, che a fine stagione potrebbero avere un peso importante.

- Il peso della Champions Qua le variabili sono tante. E si parte dal capire se Inter e Roma andranno avanti oltre la League Phase, di cui mancano ancora 4 partite. Se una dovesse andare avanti e l'altra no, inevitabilmente anche il campionato potrebbe risentirne. Ma sono discorsi prematuri, nella speranza che entrambe possano superare senza playoff questo primo turno di Champions League.

#2101. Southampton loanee has chance to kickstart his spell after Keven Schlotterbeck injury: Opinion

Southampton had a mixed summer transfer window but one major blow was the sale of Taylor Harwood-Bellis. The Saints brought in multiple defenders in a bid to replace him and one of which was Zach Abbott who joined on loan.

Abbott has a chance to change the course of his Southampton loan spell following Keven Schlotterbeck’s shoulder injury. The Nottingham Forest youngster was introduced during the 1-0 defeat at Preston North End and delivered a composed performance across 79 minutes at centre-back, earning a 6.8 FotMob rating.

It was only his second Championship appearance since arriving on loan in September, but the circumstances have created an opportunity he desperately needs. At 20, Abbott is still developing, and regular first-team football was the obvious attraction of his temporary move to St Mary’s.

Abbott has been honest about his frustration at the lack of minutes, admitting to BBC Radio Solent that he has been “itching for a lot more”. His response to limited opportunities has been to remain patient, work hard in training and take advice from his experienced teammates.

The numbers underline how little football Abbott has played. He has accumulated just 124 Championship minutes across two appearances, completing 74 of his 84 passes at an impressive 88.1% accuracy. He has also won two of his three aerial duels, with his success rate ranking in the 86th percentile among full-backs.

Although the sample size is small, his Preston performance offered encouragement that he can handle the demands of Championship football. His versatility is another advantage, having previously demonstrated an ability to operate at both centre-back and right-back.

Southampton are 7th after 15 games, with 24 points, and remain firmly in the promotion conversation. However, Schlotterbeck’s expected six-week absence leaves Tonda Eckert needing to find a reliable defensive replacement. Nathan Wood and Jack Stephens provide competition, but Abbott has already shown he can step in without looking out of place.

This is an important period for Abbott and both clubs. He joined Southampton to gain the senior experience that was difficult to secure at Nottingham Forest, but his lack of involvement has reportedly raised the possibility of a January recall.

A sustained run of appearances before the new year would change that picture considerably. It would provide Forest with the Championship experience they wanted him to gain and give Southampton another capable defensive option during a crucial period of their campaign.

The upcoming home fixture against Derby County after the international break could be particularly important. Abbott has already reached an FA Cup semi-final and featured in the Europa League, so his potential is clear.

Now he needs regular opportunities to demonstrate it at Championship level. Schlotterbeck’s injury is unfortunate, but it could be the opening Abbott has been waiting for. Southampton should give him the chance to make the most of it.

#2100. CorSport: Krösche, Hardung and three signings – Milan preparing for frantic January

AC Milan have shown both their potential and their limitations this season, leading to a desire to do business once the window reopens.

According to Corriere dello Sport (via MilanNews) this morning, the head coach Ruben Amorim has made it clear both publicly and privately that he needs deeper and more competitive squad in order to achieve consistency in results and performance levels.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

When the coach has had to rotate, the team suffers. Gerry Cardinale has promised significant reinforcements, and the first piece of the new structure will be Markus Krösche, set to become Head of Football on January 1st. But the German executive may not arrive alone.

Timmo Hardung – Krösche’s long time right-hand man at Eintracht Frankfurt and RB Leipzig – could follow him to Italy. The two have worked side by side in recent years, and Milan are considering re-creating the tried-and-tested management duo.

Should Hardung decide to leave Eintracht, the chances of him joining Milan are very real, as even Sky Germany have admitted. Meanwhile, Krösche is already working on the plans fr the future, although he’ll need to wait a few months before taking office.

In the winter window, the Rossoneri intend to acquire three players. A central defender remains the absolute priority, while a left-back is also being sought, in addition to a striker capable of acting as an alternative to Gonçalo Ramos.

The goal is therefore to increase the squad’s depth, especially given the difficulties encountered in midweek matches and with making multiple changes. No names are mentioned specifically, but the target has been set ahead of a potentially busy January.

#2098. Former Stoke City and Swansea City midfielder completes move to National League promotion hopefuls

Worthing currently sit 6th in the National League table and are eyeing up promotion to the Football League for the first time in their history. Now, they have strengthened their midfield by signing former Stoke City and Swansea City star Sam Clucas, who brings a huge amount of experience to the team.

The 36-year-old was last contracted to Shrewsbury Town, where he played 34 league fixtures last season, scoring two goals and assisting five. He was an important player in the Shrews’ squad last campaign, but his services were not extended further following the summer.

Across his career, Clucas has played in the Premier League, Championship, League One and League Two, and has featured for a multitude of clubs. Hereford, Mansfield Town, Chesterfield, Hull City, Swansea City, Stoke City, Rotherham United, Oldham Athletic, Lincoln City, Shrewsbury Town and now Worthing are the clubs Clucas has represented.

The experienced EFL star will now prepare for life in the fifth tier, with the hope of bringing an historic promotion to the Reds. Worthing are currently in the play-offs, having lost just one league match in their last 11.

Clucas’ experience will be worth its weight in gold, and he has a clear hunger to deliver success to Worthing. “I can see the vision of the club, and I want to be a part of it,” he said in the club statement confirming his arrival.

The former Premier League footballer has plied his trade in the most competitive division in the world and will bring a calm and level head to the National League side, especially as the pressure ramps up later on in the season.

The ex-Stoke City and Swansea City man has already made his debut too. He came on off the bench on Saturday as the Rebels drew 1-1 with Scunthorpe United.

Clucas has penned a one-year deal with the non-league side, but could be offered longer terms if he impresses at the club. If the move proves to be a success, then Worthing will try to tie him down for longer and prolong his playing career.

But if the former Stoke City and Swansea City man fails to hit the heights expected of him, the Reds will not be hurt by his departure next summer, given his contract length.

He has shown he can still play plenty of games after featuring 40 times across the 2025/26 campaign for Shrewsbury Town. Clucas appears to have plenty left in the tank, and he will help to bring squad depth to Worthing as the busiest time of the footballing calendar nears.

#2096. Belgio-Italia, 51 giorni dopo: dallo 0-2 dell'Olimpico al sogno di vincere il girone

Cinquantuno giorni dopo, è cambiato quasi tutto. Il 25 settembre, allo stadio Olimpico di Roma, l'Italia di Roberto Mancini perdeva 2-0 a cospetto del Belgio, cominciando nel peggiore dei modi il nuovo corso del commissario tecnico. Questa sera, alle 20.45, gli azzurri ritrovano i Diavoli Rossi allo stadio Re Baldovino di Bruxelles, con una prospettiva molto diversa: basta un pareggio per qualificarsi ai quarti di finale di Nations League, una vittoria garantirebbe addirittura il primo posto nel girone. In mezzo, tre successi e un pari, con il 3-1 rifilato giovedì alla Francia a San Siro che ha rappresentato il momento più alto di questa prima fase della seconda esperienza di Mancini alla guida della Nazionale. Da un gruppo contestato e reduce dalla mancata qualificazione al Mondiale a una squadra che, pur con tutti i suoi limiti, ha ritrovato risultati ed entusiasmo.

La partita d'andata fu una lezione piuttosto severa. Il Belgio di Mark van Bommel dominò il primo tempo, passando in vantaggio con Mika Godts al 20'. Donnarumma evitò un passivo più pesante, prima che Lukebakio chiudesse i conti al 69', proprio quando gli azzurri stavano cercando di rientrare in partita. Da allora Mancini ha progressivamente trovato una squadra più convincente: prima il 4-1 in Turchia, poi il pareggio per 1-1 in Francia e il successo per 3-1 nel ritorno contro i turchi. Infine, la vittoria di giovedì contro la nazionale di Zidane, con la doppietta di Francesco Pio Esposito e la rete di Frattesi. Il centravanti dell'Inter è il principale riferimento offensivo, mentre Mancini ha dato fiducia a diversi giovani, da Kayode a Scalvini, senza rinunciare all'esperienza dei vari Donnarumma, Barella e Tonali.

Il Belgio, però, ha già dimostrato di poter mettere in difficoltà gli azzurri. Giovedì ha vinto 2-1 in Turchia, rimontando lo svantaggio iniziale grazie alle reti di De Bruyne e De Ketelaere, e si presenta all'ultima giornata con 9 punti, uno in meno dell'Italia. Per la squadra di Van Bommel, la vittoria è l'unico risultato che può garantire il passaggio ai quarti senza dipendere dal risultato di Francia-Turchia. In palio c'è la rivincita, ma soprattutto la possibilità di chiudere al primo posto un girone che, all'indomani della sconfitta dell'Olimpico, sembrava destinato a riservare ben poche soddisfazioni.

#2095. Bristol City size up managerial candidates despite recent Michael Skubala statement

Bristol City sit 17th in the Championship table after winning only one of their last seven Championship games. Michael Skubala has come under fire with some early calls for his sacking, but chief executive Charlie Boss stated that the summer appointment will be given time to turn around the Robins’ fortunes.

Now though, reporter Alan Nixon states that City are doing background checks on potential replacements if they are forced into a decision over Skubala’s future. The hierarchy are checking into the availability and cost of possible targets, and there are funds in place to pay compensation for an in-work target.

Although the Robins have stated Skubala is getting a chance to find form, the belief is that they should be far higher up the Championship table. If form doesn’t turn and the right replacement candidate is up for grabs, the former Lincoln City boss could be moved on.

Boss didn’t say how long Skubala has got to turn around his fortunes to offer any hints untoward, but the fact that the pressure has been publicly addressed shows that Bristol City are acutely aware that they need to be doing far better than they are at present.

Unfortunately for Skubala, in the bid to find form, he’s got some tough opponents to face. Kim Hellberg’s Middlesbrough are up first after the ongoing international break ends, before an important home match against Wrexham the following Tuesday.

The Robins are back on the road at another promotion hopeful afterwards as they head to The Hawthorns to face West Brom. December then begins with a home tie against Swansea City, with clashes against Derby County and West Ham (both away) following.

It marks a tough run of fixtures for Skubala as he desperately looks to find the form to secure his Ashton Gate position.

Bristol City have a squad capable of far more than 17th in the Championship. The likes of Scott Twine and Jason Knight are both star players at this level, while Rio Cardines has impressed on loan from Crystal Palace and big money was spent on Dom Ballard and Lorent Tolaj.

It means that pressure on Skubala is justified, but the club are taking a smart approach in holding fire on sacking the boss for now. With new chief executive Boss, sporting director James Ellis and the new manager, it is the start of a real refresh at Ashton Gate as they hope to build towards long-term success.

A lot of work went into hiring Skubala from Lincoln City as they deduced him to be the perfect candidate to lead this new chapter. More was expected of the manager in the short term, but he will be judged on long-term results, so it is only right that he is given time to get out of this rut.

If it comes as any reassurance, Skubala endured a tough start with Lincoln. He won only two of his first 14 games, but he was given time to recover and built them into a League One title-winning side.

Bristol City will hope for a similar turnaround, but if it doesn’t come, they will be ready to act.

#2094. Expected Points and clinical shooting: Stats highlight worries about sustainability of Milan’s Serie A form

AC Milan have collected more points than they deserved so far in the 2026-27 Serie A season, according to statistical data.

As MilanPress write, the Expected Points ranking makes for worrying reading. The metric compares the points actually earned by Serie A teams with those expected based on performances and chances created and conceded in the first 11 rounds of the league season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri have earned 24 points compared to approximately 17 expected, meaning they are ‘over-performing’ by seven points. Milan are currently fourth in the table behind Lazio, Inter and Roma, but they should be a few places lower.

Inter are second with 28 actual points, but should have collected around 26, while Juventus are on 18 points earned versus the expected 21. Napoli also obtained less than the data indicated they should have, with 15 actual points compared to the approximately 19 expected.

The numbers, therefore, reveal a Milan that is particularly effective in turning its performances into tangible results. This is a positive aspect in terms of the league table, but also food for thought. Is it sustainable moving forwards?

Another interesting statistic has come from Kickest, which perhaps highlights why Ruben Amorim’s side have been able to out-perform what the data suggests.

They reveal that there are 113 players with at least 10 shots in Serie A so far in 2026-27. The top four with the best conversion rates have something in common: they play for the Diavolo.

➤ Rabiot — 41.7% (5 goals) ➤ Moreira — 40.0% (4) ➤ Cisse — 38.5% (5) ➤ Pulisic — 36.4% (4) ➤ De Bruyne — 30.0% (3)

It is reminiscent of something we published in January, when the shooting numbers under Massimiliano Allegri were similarly remarkable. As we know, a late-season collapse ended up coming.

Then there was the revelation from Sky after the Genoa game, as they looked at data per 30 minutes of possession. Milan are first in Serie A for build-up actions, but they are 20th for entries into the final third and entries into the opposition box.

Amorim’s side are 19th for percentage of touches in the attacking third and 18th in percentage of touches in the opposition box. So, Milan must get much better at generating and sustaining pressure, or the results might start to regress.

#2092. Premier League star's miscarriage heartbreak: Fulham striker Rodrigo Muniz reveals off-field agony in emotional interview - before sharing his wife is pregnant again

Published: 06:24 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 04:12 EST, 9 November 2026

Fulham striker Rodrigo Muniz has opened up on his 'really difficult' off-field issues, with the Brazilian revealing he and his wife suffered a miscarriage last year.

Muniz, 25, earned the Cottagers a point in Saturday's draw against Newcastle, with his 83rd minute strike his first Premier League goal since August 2025.

The centre forward, speaking with club media after the Craven Cottage game, spoke candidly of the difficulties he has faced with wife Jady - who are now expecting again after a turbulent year.

'Last season was really difficult for me because, now I can say, I had surgery, my wife was pregnant last season but unfortunately we lost the baby,' he said.

'But God is good all the time and now she is pregnant again. The goal was for my baby and I hope this season will be different to last season.'

Fulham star Rodrigo Muniz opened up on his personal agony after scoring on Saturday

Muniz revealed his wife Jady suffered a miscarriage but they are now pregnant again

Muniz has not been afforded a start by new Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa, making all eight of his Premier League appearances off the bench so far this season.

He hopes that his contribution against the Toon has done enough to earn his manager's trust after the international break.

'I train hard every week to get opportunities to play and I want to play more,' he said.

'I cannot control that but I showed to the gaffer I want to play more.

'And I have to keep training hard for him to say, 'okay, now is your time', and then I'm ready.

'To be a striker, you need to be ready to play five or ten minutes. Of course, I want to play more. And I want to start as well.

'We have a lot of players in the national team. We train with, I think, ten players.

'And when we have time to work it's really good – because it's really important that the gaffer can show us what he wants and we have time to do it.'

#2091. GdS: A start vs. France at San Siro – Cisse’s rapid ascent continues with Mancini’s faith

Alphadjo Cisse continues to go from strength to strength, and his biggest moment yet might be coming during the break.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, beyond the confidence with which he plays and speaks, what’s truly striking is Cisse’s composure in front of goal at just 20 years of age, experiencing his first proper season in the top flight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

His goal in Genoa seemed easy because he made it so, but it wasn’t. Adrien Rabiot’s pass was quite slow, the distance to the goal wasn’t that close, Genoa were exposed after losing the ball but Bijlow wasn’t in a particularly bad position, and beating him required precision.

Other strikers in those circumstances may have opted for a powerful finish. Not Cisse. He looked for the corner and found it with a lovely precise strike, one which revealed everything about the groove he has found himself in.

It was goal number five in the league for Alphadjo Cisse, making him Milan’s joint-top scorer alongside Rabiot. That extends to eight across all competitions, which puts the young Italian alone on the pedastal.

Two stats in particular stand out. The first: with his fifth goal in his ninth league appearance at 20 years and 17 days, he became the second-youngest Rossoneri player to reach this milestone in his first 10 appearances in the three-points-for-a-win era, after Pato (18 years and 181 days).

Second: he is one of only three players born in 2006 or later in the five major European leagues in 2026-27 to have scored at least eight goals in all competitions, along with Yamal (13) and Brunner (8).

Oh, and there’s another pretty good one: Shevchenko also scored eight goals in his first 13 games of the season with the Diavolo (although he achieved this in fewer minutes). The reward could well be a renewal, to fend off Premier League interest too.

🇮🇹 “The San Siro boys. Esposito plus Cissé: Mancini looks to a Milanese Italy.”

🤔 “Esposito is a lock at centre-forward, the debutant Alphadjo could join him in the attacking trio against France. Could Zaniolo be there too?” pic.twitter.com/zCkNmyqISY

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 10, 2026

Now, a change in dressing room awaits over the break. Roberto Mancini called him up to the senior national team for the first time, and according to La Gazzetta, the talent could start immediately.

He’s currently competing for a spot on the left in the 4-3-3 formation with Cambiaghi and Sebastiano Esposito. The Rossoneri guarantees more presence in the penalty area and quality in finishing, while Cambiaghi provides more coverage.

We’ll see if Mancini ultimately chooses to use him from the start, but what’s certain is that the former Verona man will be ready no matter what, and for a game at San Siro against France no less.

#2090. Two positions West Ham boss Scott Parker wants to strengthen in the January transfer window

West Ham opted for change earlier this month as they parted ways with Nuno Espirito Santo to bring in Scott Parker as boss. The former three-time WHUFC Player of the Year will be expected to deliver improvements with his current squad, but new signings will be sought in the winter transfer window too.

According to Alan Nixon, the Hammers’ boss is eager to add new options at left-back and striker when January comes around. His preference is to sign a centre-forward with Championship experience, while a ‘specialist’ is left full-back is sought given that Morato is primarily a centre-back while Ezra Mayers and Ollie Scarles are only young.

Parker has tasked scouts with finding standout targets in both positions and the money is there to spend. It remains to be seen just who emerges on the radar with around six weeks until the window opens.

Parker hasn’t even been at West Ham for two weeks, but he already has a good idea of where they need to strengthen if they are to achieve their goal of promotion back to the Premier League.

And, with reinforcements sought at striker and left-back, many supporters will be behind the boss too. Striker has been a problem area with none of Joel Piroe, Taty Castellanos or Pablo proving they can be the Hammers’ leading talisman as of yet.

There are options at left-back, but Morato felt very much like a Nuno player given their past spell together at Nottingham Forest. His defence-first game suited the former boss’ style too.

Youngsters Mayers and Scarles may hope to prove they can step up for Parker, but a specialist left-back would not go amiss. It could also mean the writing is on the wall for Adama Boiro, who has not played since his debut on September 5th.

Parker has won three promotions from the Championship, and he is targeting a fourth with West Ham. Given his past success, the club hierarchy will be more than willing to put faith in his transfer opinions ahead of January.

WHUFC seem set to heed his advice and target reinforcements at both striker and left-back ahead of January. There are already plenty of players in these positions, but with neither locked down by a clear standout, there is a need for ruthlessness in upgrading in both areas.

Not only will it strengthen the squad, but it will help Parker make his mark too. Players signed specifically for his setup and tactics will be backed to come in and make a swift impact as the Hammers take action in the bid to win promotion.

#2088. AFC Wimbledon vs Blackpool “shouldn’t have taken place”, says Ian Evatt after sickness-hit squad loses 1-0

Blackpool fell to a narrow 1-0 defeat against fellow strugglers AFC Wimbledon, with Alistair Smith netting the all-important goal in the 13th minute with a sublime strike from distance.

To say the Tangerines’ preparations for the trip to South London were disrupted would be an understatement. Ian Evatt’s group was ravaged by a sickness bug, leaving 14 players and staff absent. Bailey Peacock-Farrell and Josh Bowler, two positives in an otherwise tough campaign, were two notable absentees at Plough Lane.

Speaking after the game, Evatt admitted he had never encountered anything quite like it as he spoke to the club’s media channels. He said: “I don’t want to be stood here and feel like I am making excuses; I can only tell the truth. We’ve had 14 players and staff have severe diarrhoea and vomiting for the last 24 hours – it started as soon as we got on the train yesterday, and it spiralled quickly.

“Some players and staff haven’t been able to get out of bed, but they put themselves forward to come on the pitch and play today. For me, we’ve been put in a position we shouldn’t have been put into and this game shouldn’t have taken place today and I would have been saying that if we had won the game.”

The game had a COVID-19 feel with the two sides emerging from the tunnel separately and skipping the customary pre-match handshakes.

Nonetheless, Evatt’s Blackpool dominated for large spells and should have taken at least a point back up to Lancashire, but they couldn’t beat the inspired Nathan Bishop in the Dons’ net.

The energetic performance was a testament to the character of Blackpool in challenging circumstances. They mustered 15 attempts on goal compared to AFC Wimbledon’s nine and created over double their opponents’ xG at 1.22 (FotMob).

They failed to take advantage of the several opportunities they had though, with Dale Taylor and Tom Bloxham struggling to make an impact leading the line.

Returning to Bloomfield Road last October after seven years as a player, Evatt is arguably facing one of his most challenging periods in the dugout.

He managed to steer Blackpool away from relegation last term, although not convincingly, but inconsistency this term has once again left them languishing at the wrong end of the table.

Following a bright start with wins over Stockport County and Peterborough United, a run of just one victory in 10 league outings has put the Seasiders in a very familiar position and staring down the barrel of another relegation dogfight.

Evatt raised his stock considerably at Bolton Wanderers but is yet to make his mark at Blackpool, with the visit of in-form Wigan Athletic next Saturday potentially proving decisive in his long-term future.

#2087. Celtic fans disgracefully boo during minute's silence on Remembrance Sunday: Referee ends tribute after just 13 SECONDS - even after warning from the PA announcer

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 03:28 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 04:51 EST, 9 November 2026

Celtic were forced to curtail plans to commemorate Remembrance Day after a section of their supporters booed during the planned minute's silence on Remembrance Sunday.

The Bhoys hosted Kilmarnock in the Scottish Premiership on Sunday - with Liam Scales' goal proving the difference in a 1-0 win.

However, ahead of kick-off at Parkhead, the annual tribute to the armed forces and their families was overshadowed by some fans' loud jeers.

As the players from both teams gathered around the centre-circle, an announcement on the public address system said: 'We will have a minute's silence today on Remembrance Sunday to remember all victims of all conflicts. We remember, in particular, the men who served Celtic football club and lost their lives at wartime.'

The audible disdain resulted in referee John Beaton being forced to cut the silence after just 13 seconds.

The noise was so palpable that the Celtic TV broadcast turned down the volume to try and minimise its impact too.

The minute's silence ahead of Celtic versus Kilmarnock was cut short due to some fans booing

Celtic TV turned down the volume to try and minimise the jeers during the curtailed silence

Referee John Beaton (right) cut the minute's silence after 13 seconds as a result of the booing

Furthermore, the lower tier of the standing section was empty until the Green Brigade and other fans started to file in from the concourse when referee Beaton’s whistle signalled the end of the tribute.

Football clubs across the United Kingdom observe a minute's silence with their nearest home fixture around Remembrance Sunday and Armistice Day - with the latter on November 11.

Many teams also wear poppies, something Kilmarnock wore on their strip, but Celtic didn't.

Some Celtic supporters refuse to partake in the tradition or actively take a stance against it, often citing the club’s Irish roots and linking it to the British Army‘s role in The Troubles.

Last season, in a quirk, Celtic hosted Kilmarnock on Remembrance Sunday too - with that minute's silence also cut short due to jeering. That time referee Don Robertson cut it short at 15 seconds.

As well as the booing in that match last term, some fans turned their back on the minute's silence and also made gestures.

Sunday's 1-0 win over Kilmarnock sees Celtic regain their four-point lead at the top of the Scottish Premiership.

It was under-pressure Martin O'Neill's side's first league win in their last three games.

Scales scored the only goal of the game on 26 minutes when he hooked a Camilo Duran cross into the top corner.

Celtic fans show their displeasure during the minute's silence for Remembrance Day in 2025

Celtic - and Kasper Hogh in particular - otherwise had a frustrating day in front of goal, with Benjamin Nygren missing a second-half penalty.

Hogh had an early goal disallowed as his barren run without a goal hit the 16-game mark since he netted a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on his second appearance.

Celtic have 31 points from their opening 13 matches - four more than bitter rivals Rangers who sit second but have a game in hand.

Kilmarnock remain rooted to the bottom of the table with nine points from 13 games - two adrift of 11th-place Aberdeen who have played a match fewer.

Derby County have had a tough season to date, but they entered the international break on a high by beating Bolton Wanderers 3-1 at Pride Park. It gives DCFC fans some renewed hope, and might have saved John Eustace his job as well.

The Rams have been way under par, but injuries have torn through the squad and played a big part in their struggles. Eustace’s defence has been heavily impacted especially, and among those sidelined has been Eiran Cashin.

But, in a welcome boost, the Brighton & Hove Albion loanee has been back in training over the first week of the international break. Cashin may need a little more time before he gets back to full fitness, but once deemed ready, he should come straight back into their starting lineup.

Cashin was a popular signing in the summer transfer window. The 25-year-old is a product of the Derby County academy and left to join Brighton in January 2025, but has struggled to make the grade at the Premier League club and spent spells on loan back in the Championship as a result.

He didn’t impress as hoped at Birmingham City, but offered a timely reminder of how good he can be at the level during his stay at Blackburn Rovers. Cashin helped the Lancashire outfit steer clear of relegation last season before reuniting with the Rams for the 2026/27 campaign.

The Irishman has only played twice for DCFC since his return due to this calf injury, but he will be backed to land a key role when fit and available. He’s a dependable and busy defender at this level, with his 3.26 tackles per 90 last season more than any other Championship defender.

Cashin also managed 12.96 defensive contributions, 9.33 duels won, and 14.94 line-breaking passes per 90, ranking among the league’s best in these metrics too (FotMob). He’ll offer Eustace an option at left-back and centre-back, and give the boss the option to switch to a back three as well.

He will bring more balance to the backline as a left-footer and has the love for defending that has been coached out of some modern-day centre-backs.

The Bolton Wanderers win was only one victory, but it will hopefully mark a big step in the right direction. It lifts a weight off the shoulders of Eustace and his Derby County players coming into the break.

This paired with the improving injury picture should give DCFC hope that they can start to find some form. Not only is Cashin back in training, but Patrick Agyemang and Matt Clarke featured in the behind-closed-doors friendly at Everton on Thursday as well.

With defensive depth and key players returning, the Rams will be targeting some valuable points to push up the Championship table and away from the relegation zone.

#2082. Some are calling this 'Tuchel 2.0' and his latest squad does feel like that. Here's why England think a tilt at the European Championship is within reach, writes IAN LADYMAN

Published: 17:35 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 05:45 EST, 9 November 2026

One of Thomas Tuchel’s favourite analogies when it comes to the development of his England team is that of a train leaving a station with only the chosen few on it. As time moves on, the bodies lying on the tracks are growing greater in number.

Consider this statistic. Of the 26 players who travelled to the World Cup in America 13 are not in the squad chosen by England manager Tuchel for next week’s Nations League games against Croatia and Spain. And that does not include Cole Palmer and Phil Foden who, after missing out in the summer, were expected by many of us to have forced a way back in by now.

Tuchel’s latest selection has been affected by injuries, of course. But more significant is that the experienced German believes he is now starting to see an England team and squad develop in a way and in a direction that even he hadn’t envisaged once Argentina ended his World Cup hopes in that dismal Atlanta semi-final in July.

Different feelings, different style of play and, to a degree, different players.

Some are calling this ‘Tuchel 2.0’ and it does feel a little bit like that. The start of the second phase of Tuchel’s tenure, the start of the road towards a tilt at another trophy, the European Championships of 2028.

Having admitted to some worry ahead of the four-game international break FIFA saddled us all with last month, Tuchel sat down yesterday looking and sounding like a man once again certain of himself.

Tuchel sat down with the media looking and sounding like a man once again certain of himself

The inclusion of Jobe Bellingham — Jude’s younger brother (right) — was the headline act but there were other messages written within

Certain enough of a direct, quick, athletic style of play that helped England to two wins over Czech Republic and one – by seven goals – against Croatia in Rijeka. And certain that a dependence on players like Jordan Henderson, Dan Burn and John Stones for what we may politely call ‘squad culture management’ lies now in the past.

All of this may crash down in Madrid next Sunday. Spain have already beaten Tuchel’s England once – at Wembley in late September – and a repeat this month would ask familiar questions about England against the really good teams.

But for now, Tuchel is confident enough to claim that he has found his path.

‘We said at some point we need to take the next step, to build on what we have, to get better and to improve otherwise you’re just left behind,’ said Tuchel yesterday.

‘That’s how football works. You have been champion in one season but you need to improve, you need to bring in new players for competition, young players, new energy, fresh energy. It’s also the way, naturally, the national team goes.

‘We cannot be stuck in the same personnel and in the same style of play.

‘I agreed with you last month. I was the first to admit I was not 100 per cent happy with the pure level of football we played in the US. I saw a higher level in training [than on the field], I saw a higher level in glimpses.

‘We adjusted some things tactically, created some new positions and took the next steps.’

The Tuchel we sat down with in late September still wore the scars of the summer’s disappointment – and the criticism that came with it – rather visibly. It was the first time we had seen him like that in his two years in the job. He was tetchy and easily provoked. Call it the Argentina effect if you like.

Here, he appeared rather healed. Good results tend to do that for a manager and a little time helps too. If he believes his team has moved on then maybe he has also and he had to.

Certainly, his selection squad speaks to that. The inclusion of Jobe Bellingham – Jude’s younger brother – was the headline act but there were other messages written within.

Henderson and Burn are available but not included. So too Arsenal’s Noni Madueke, excluded to the benefit of the more direct Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha.

‘We need runners who will go between the lines,’ said Tuchel. A clear indication, there, that too much of England’s summer wing play was too slow and too conservatively narrow.

Palmer, Foden and Kobbie Mainoo are also on the outside looking in once again and the case of the Manchester United midfielder is perhaps indicative of how Tuchel now operates.

Moved to apologise to him in front of the whole squad in July for his lack of minutes at the World Cup, Tuchel was determined Mainoo would play in the opening four games of the Nations League campaign.

‘I was desperate to give him the minutes and desperate to include him in this new start,’ explained Tuchel.

‘But then he pulled out. He missed an excellent camp and also entered a difficult, difficult spell for himself.

‘Man United fell off a cliff a little bit performance-wise. So this is why he now suffers.’

We can talk about the whys and wherefores of that logic. If Mainoo was good enough in September then why is he not good enough now? How desperate could Tuchel really have been to play him that one withdrawal with injury closed the door for the next camp and opened it instead for Bellingham jnr?

This, though, is how Tuchel works. He is an adept tactician but he’s also a mood coach, someone who – after sobering club experiences at places like PSG, Chelsea and Bayern Munich – places huge emphasis on environments and gut feels and culture. If he feels something works, he doesn’t like to pick it apart without good reason.

This is why for example the growing voice and influence of Elliot Anderson has left Jordan Henderson suddenly surplus. Tuchel says the door is not closed on a player who will be 38 by the time the next Euros are played and he called him this week to say so. In Tuchel’s mind, though, England will now move without the veteran and others of his ilk.

‘I was concerned before the last camp that we missed the players who kept our standards,’ said Tuchel.

‘I was worried that we missed so many of them. But then this group found their own way and their own voices.

It’s also reasonable to ask why our head coach can’t find room in his squad – if not his team – for the game changing duo of Palmer and Foden

‘I know what the others did. They built a platform on which these ones can build.’

Time will tell. To a degree, Spain will tell. Can England play the kind of higher tempo, front foot football we saw against Croatia and the Czechs against the world and European champions next Sunday? They embarrassed us when we didn’t have the ball at Wembley.

It’s also reasonable to ask why our head coach can’t find room in his squad – if not his team – for the game-changing duo of Palmer and Foden. England lacked good substitutes at the World Cup. There was too much like for like.

England need to win in order for such decisions to be vindicated and Tuchel knows that.

Asked yesterday if he felt as invigorated as he looked he said he did. ‘The last camp gave me a lot of energy, gave me a lot of extra belief,’ he said.

‘It gave me a lot of optimism to not compromise on the way England teams should play. Be physical but also step up in the pure level of performances.’

It’s certainly time for this now. The summer only served to expose English shortcomings. Tuchel’s train must arrive in Madrid next weekend, not only with fresh personnel but also new ideas clearly apparent.

#2081. Sheffield Wednesday & Sunderland won’t be surprised by Ashley Fletcher, Huddersfield Town situation

Ashley Fletcher's two years at Blackpool indicated that his best years may still be ahead of him, but so far at Huddersfield Town, he's showing inconsistencies that the likes of Sunderland and Sheffield Wednesday know all too well.

The 31-year-old has been one of the more frustrating frontmen in the EFL over the past decade or so.

Fletcher had a massively bright future coming out of the Manchester United academy, but couldn't realise his Premier League potential at West Ham United during his sole campaign at the London Stadium. In 2017, he moved to Middlesbrough and, barring an 11-goal, seven-assist campaign in 2019/20, struggled to make an impact in the Championship.

However, dropping down to League One with Blackpool a couple of years ago seemed to be the catalyst for some productive campaigns, registering 19 goal involvements in his first season in Tangerine and following that up with 21 goals in all competitions last season.

Unfortunately, he hasn't been able to carry that momentum in West Yorkshire.

With Fletcher's Blackpool contract running out at the end of last season, all eyes were on where the 31-year-old would go.

He'd shown himself to be at least a top-end League One striker, and despite the Seasiders' ambitions, it was his goals which stopped what would have been a disastrous relegation to the fourth tier. If anything, his decision to leave was accepted at Bloomfield Road.

Huddersfield were the side to snap him up, announcing a deal at the start of June, before his contract with Blackpool even expired. The haste in the deal indicated that the 31-year-old was going to be a big player for Martin Drury this season, but that hasn't been the case so far.

Fletcher has continued to be a good link-up striker, someone who holds the ball up as well as anyone in his position, but his finishing ability hasn't followed him from Blackpool.

He has just two league goals in 720 minutes of action, from an expected goals tally of 3.25. One of his efforts this season saw him tackle Burton Albion goalkeeper Corey Addai into the net in their 3-1 win last month, too — not exactly a clinical finish.

With Bojan Radulovic boasting better scoring stats in around 250 fewer minutes, it may only be a matter of time before the Serbian replaces Fletcher once he's back to full fitness, which would be a big disappointment given the excitement surrounding the 31-year-old's arrival.

Fletcher's inconsistencies in front of goal will make Sunderland fans remember his loan spell at the Stadium of Light back during the second half of the 2017/18 campaign, their first back in the Championship, and what would end up being their second of back-to-back relegations.

The then-22-year-old was brought in on loan from fellow second-tier outfit Middlesbrough to help drag an endangered Sunderland side out of the bottom three, but he massively underwhelmed.

The Black Cats didn't win any of his first eight games at the club, dropping to the foot of the second-tier table, before his first goal on March 30 led to a rare win against play-off-chasing Derby County.

That didn't end up being a catalyst for a great escape, though, as Sunderland would win just one more game that year, with Fletcher scoring just once more, too. Coincidentally, they both occurred in the same game, against Champions Wolves on the final day, with his side already relegated.

A difficult loan spell in troubling circumstances; Fletcher could have become a Sunderland hero, but instead struggled to make an impact.

Fast forward five years from that Sunderland relegation, Fletcher was under contract at Watford, but the Hornets, despite being a Championship club, weren't interested in having him lead their line.

He was loaned out to three different sides during his time at Vicarage Road, the third of which came with Sheffield Wednesday in the 2023/24 campaign — their first back in the second tier following their miraculous play-off win under Darren Moore.

What followed was, at the time, the worst Championship start ever, with Xisco Munoz sacked after 10 games with no wins, and it wouldn't be until their 14th league outing that Wednesday picked up their first three points of the campaign.

Fletcher was around the squad, but never really started enough games to make an impact, and the same could be said during the early stages of Danny Rohl's time at Hillsborough.

Come the end of the January transfer window, the frontman was starting to be left out of matchday squads, until a mid-February match against Millwall saw Fletcher subbed on with 11 minutes to go, before picking up two stoppage-time yellow cards and being sent off.

That proved to be his final appearance for Wednesday. He failed to score in his 23 Championship appearances, and it was from there that he dropped into League One with Blackpool.

Ultimately, we are only 14 games into the new season, and Fletcher is part of a Huddersfield squad flying high with plenty of capable goalscorers, so he's not the only person relied upon to find the net at his new club.

But with a few wasted chances already, it's hard not to hear alarm bells, given his past before that switch to Blackpool.

Martin Drury's side are in a great position in the League One title race during this international break, and if Fletcher can find his form again, they could be nearly unstoppable.

Bradford City are being targeted by a Thai-based consortium over a potential takeover bid, which could make for an interesting few weeks ahead.

Journalist Alan Nixon revealed that the Bantams are subject to interest from a consortium from Thailand. Bradford are currently in League One, and will be looking to win promotion into the Championship this term under the management of newly-appointed boss, Michael Duff.

Nixon revealed that the group interested in taking over Bradford have held previous interest in other EFL clubs, and so it remains to be seen as to whether they'll make a breakthrough this time around with the third-tier club.
